# Best portable power stations for a CPAP

The reviews I found are mostly spec-based runtime math, not hands-on testing. A CPAP draws little power (about 30-40 W, or 60-90 W with a heated humidifier), so the real question is how many nights you want per charge.

## My picks

**Best overall: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** (about $700)
- It has 1,024 Wh, a 10 ms UPS switchover, and is rated at about 20 dB under 200 W, so it's quiet by the bed.
- Tested Watts estimates about 2.7 nights without a humidifier and about 1.7 with one. It also has the fastest wall recharge in their group (~49 min).
- Details: [Tested Watts guide](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/). Buy links are on [BuyerSheet's CPAP list](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/).

**Best value for runtime: Bluetti AC180** ($449-$499)
- It has 1,152 Wh, which BuyerSheet estimates at about 3.1 nights dry and 1.4 with a humidifier.
- The downsides are weight (about 35 lb per BuyerSheet) and a 20 ms UPS switchover, slower than the Anker's. If a CPAP must never blink during an outage, confirm that with your machine's maker.
- The listed price is $499 with a code, AFF5OFF, taking $24.95 off to $474.05. PowerStationBench shows $449 on Amazon, so compare before buying.
- [Buy at BLUETTI's official US store (affiliate link, the site earns a commission at no cost to you)](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). Specs are on the [Dealectric page](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180).

**Best budget for two dry nights: EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro** ($389)
- It has about 2.0 nights dry and 0.9 with a humidifier, per [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/). It weighs 18.2 lb.
- The Bluetti Elite 100 mini ($429, about 2.7 nights dry) is another option on the same page.

**Best for travel: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (about $499)
- It's the lightest 1 kWh pick at 23.8 lb, with about 1.75 humidified nights per Tested Watts. Buy links are on [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/).

**Smallest and cheapest: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus** ($279-$299)
- At 286 Wh it covers a single night only if you skip the heated humidifier. With one, it's under a night ([Outage Power Guide](https://outagepowerguide.com/reviews/best-power-station-for-cpap-machines/)).

## Before you buy
- **Check your machine's draw.** A heated humidifier roughly halves your runtime, so I'd buy for the humidified numbers if you use one.
- **Use pure sine wave output or your CPAP's DC cord.** All the stations above meet this. The 12 V car port plus your CPAP maker's DC converter can stretch runtime.
- **Plan for outages longer than one night.** I'd aim for at least two nights at your settings.
- **This isn't medical advice.** If you depend on therapy, talk to your provider or equipment supplier about a backup plan.

If you tell me your CPAP model, whether you use the humidifier, and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
